questions.question: Can a non-executive director of a private sector bank give instructions directly to bank employees or branch managers on operational matters?
questions.answer: No, a non-executive director has no individual power to act on behalf of the bank or give directions to employees; any instructions must be routed through the MD&CEO or CEO.
questions.evidence: a NED as an individual, shall have no power to act on behalf of the PVB nor can they give any direction to the employees of the PVB on behalf of the management. A NED shall desist from sending any instructions to the individual officers on any matters

questions.question: What must a non-executive director do if they have a direct or indirect interest in a contract or loan being discussed by the board of a private sector bank?
questions.answer: The director must disclose the nature of their interest to the board as soon as possible and must not vote on that contract, loan, arrangement, or proposal unless their presence is required by other directors to elicit information.
questions.evidence: a NED who is directly or indirectly concerned or interested in any contract, loan, arrangement or proposal entered into or proposed to be entered by or on behalf of the banking company shall, as soon as possible after the relevant circumstances have come to their knowledge, disclose the nature of their interest to the Board

unanswerable.question: Within how many calendar days must a non-executive director disclose their interest in a contract or loan after becoming aware of it?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states disclosure must be made 'as soon as possible' but does not specify a numeric deadline or calendar day limit.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank charge fees for additional facilities offered in a Basic Savings Bank Deposit account?
questions.answer: Yes, a commercial bank may provide additional facilities in a BSBD account with or without charges, as long as it is done in a non-discretionary and non-discriminatory manner with transparent disclosure.
questions.evidence: A bank may provide additional facilities beyond the above minimum in a BSBD account, with or without charges, in a non-discretionary and non-discriminatory manner with transparent disclosure to the customer.

questions.question: Is a commercial bank allowed to require a minimum balance in a BSBD account when the customer opts for additional facilities?
questions.answer: No, the bank shall not require the customer to maintain a minimum balance in the BSBD account even when additional facilities are availed.
questions.evidence: However, while doing so, the bank shall not require the customer to maintain a minimum balance in the BSBD account.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of additional facilities a commercial bank can offer in a BSBD account under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any limit on the number of additional facilities a bank may provide.

questions.question: Does a commercial bank's outsourcing arrangement reduce or alter its customers' legal rights against the bank?
questions.answer: No, outsourcing arrangements cannot affect customers' rights against the bank, including their ability to seek redressal under applicable laws.
questions.evidence: Outsourcing arrangements entered into by a bank shall not affect the rights of its customers against the bank, including the ability of the customers to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.

questions.question: Can customers of a commercial bank still pursue redressal for issues arising from outsourced services?
questions.answer: Yes, customers retain their ability to obtain redressal under relevant laws regardless of any outsourcing arrangement the bank has entered into.
questions.evidence: Outsourcing arrangements entered into by a bank shall not affect the rights of its customers against the bank, including the ability of the customers to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time limit a commercial bank has to resolve a customer complaint related to an outsourced service?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that outsourcing must not affect customers' redressal rights under relevant laws, but it does not specify any time limit, deadline, or procedural timeline for complaint resolution.
